questions: Verify least-privilege tool restrictions, schema validation and untrusted advice boundaries.
Compare deterministic monitoring with event-triggered model diagnosis and cheap fallback chains.
decision: Keep observation deterministic by default and invoke one bounded, genuinely read-only advisory pass only for novel ambiguity; treat its output as expiring untrusted data.
code_observations: assistant_triage has a strict advice schema, eligibility triggers and a capsule that does not authoritatively change task state. observer adds a separate restricted diagnostic route.
assistant_triage.evidence slices command/head/tail before calling redact, despite the redactor's intended redact-before-truncate contract. Boundary-sensitive sanitation needs a regression test.
Tool restrictions and startup guards are code-level controls; a summary prompt alone cannot enforce read-only behavior.

symbols.name: ## Native profiles and the important limitation

implementation_steps: Move sanitation ahead of any truncation of model-facing data, including command strings, output windows and failure summaries. Test split credential/header cases.

Keep explicit diagnostics local: syntax/lint errors, known missing tools and clear health failures do not need a model. Trigger one bounded diagnosis only for ambiguous stagnation or repeated unclear evidence.
Qualify each observer fallback for true read-only/no-tool or restricted-tool execution. Missing confinement disables the candidate rather than escalating its permissions.
Validate advice schema, finite confidence, allowed evidence IDs and byte limits. Label hypotheses unverified and bind the capsule to the next eligible attempt only.
Record advisory invocation cost separately and never let advice complete tasks, edit files, choose authoritative failure classes or delete evidence.
Invoke advice only for a new unresolved anomaly and cap attempts, input/output size and permitted tools.
Redact before truncation and bind suggestions to evidence generation; consume once as unverified data.
Skip advisory routes lacking proven read-only enforcement while preserving deterministic monitoring.
proposed_acceptance_tests: Clear deterministic errors invoke no advisory model.
A planted Authorization header or long secret split at a prior slice boundary is redacted before prompt construction.
Unknown evidence IDs, extra JSON fields, non-finite confidence and oversized hypotheses are rejected.
Unavailable cheap observer falls back only to another allowed restricted observer, otherwise skips.
Advice cannot mutate route/status and expires after its intended attempt.
A healthy run and repeated identical anomaly trigger no extra model calls.
A token spanning excerpt boundaries is removed before serialization.
A suggestion that requests commands, writes or status changes is rejected as data outside its role.
An old-generation suggestion cannot affect a new attempt.

alternatives.title: Continuous model log watcher
alternatives.tradeoff: Flexible free-text reasoning; Expensive and excessive privilege/context. Reject

alternatives.title: Only deterministic monitoring
alternatives.tradeoff: Cheapest and predictable; May leave ambiguous diagnosis. Default

alternatives.title: One event-triggered read-only advisor
alternatives.tradeoff: Useful bounded second opinion; Needs genuine confinement and freshness. Optional recommendation

alternatives.title: Advisor can repair and mark complete
alternatives.tradeoff: Fewer role transitions; Breaks independent acceptance and authority. Reject

cost_model: Advisor cost is justified only when expected avoided diagnosis/repair cost exceeds the call and anchoring risk under the quality floor. Use zero model tokens for routine health/progress.
unverified: Actual sandbox enforcement and account-specific observer economics require authorized live qualification. This report does not certify any hosted model as universally read-only.
No observer was dispatched. Read-only eligibility requires adapter/host tests, not this report or a provider marketing label.
runtime_experiments: No authenticated provider invocation, live quota/cost benchmark, independent model review, or Windows runtime test was performed in this research revision.
previous_decision: Use deterministic monitoring by default and event-triggered, read-only, untrusted diagnostic advice with bounded fallback.
revision_delta: The new compatibility evidence removes prompt-only or misleading safe-mode assumptions. The revision adds cross-chunk redaction, freshness binding and a zero-model-cost healthy path.
decision_analysis: An observer should not be another autonomous implementer with the same filesystem privileges. First collect deterministic exit, health and progress evidence; only an unresolved anomaly with a new fingerprint can justify a bounded advisory call. Repeated healthy polling, repeated identical failures and unavailable observer models should not spend tokens.

The advisory packet should contain whitelisted metadata, bounded sanitized excerpts and assigned file references, not the full repository, environment or historical transcript. Redact before taking head/tail slices. Bind the result to task, attempt, code/evidence generation and anomaly signature so old advice cannot leak into a later unrelated failure.

Read-only is an enforced capability: tool allowlists, filesystem restrictions and network policy must support it. Provider defaults, plan-mode prompts and sandbox names are insufficient. The adapter skips unsupported advice safely and retains deterministic diagnosis. Do not downgrade the implementation capability or widen permissions merely to obtain an observer response.

A schema-valid suggestion can still be wrong or malicious. Validate allowed fields and path references, label hypotheses unverified, and prohibit the advisor from changing authoritative classification, route, status or acceptance. The implementation worker verifies the hypothesis against evidence; advice is consumed once and expires.
